prompt:
Add a gap report for station exports. It runs as `python -m stationlog.gaps INPUT_CSV [--max-minutes N]`. INPUT_CSV is a station export like the ones the package already reads, and rows that cannot be parsed are skipped the same way.

For each station, look at its readings in time order. A gap is a pair of consecutive readings of the same station that are more than a limit apart. With --max-minutes N, the limit is N minutes for every station. Without it, the limit for a station is 3 times the median interval between its consecutive readings (for an even number of intervals, the median is the mean of the two middle ones). A station with fewer than 2 readings has no gaps. Other code should be able to run the gap search on a list of readings, either with a fixed limit or with the limit left out.

The result goes to a CSV file named `<name>.gaps.csv` in the same folder as INPUT_CSV, where <name> is the input file name without its extension (north.csv gives north.gaps.csv). It has the header `station,start,end,minutes` and one row per gap, ordered by station and then by start. start and end are the times of the two readings as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, and minutes is the length of the gap as a whole number. The file is written even if no gap is found.

Tell the user about each station that has more than 5 gaps, and at the end tell the user how many gaps were found in how many stations.

If INPUT_CSV does not exist, if it lacks one of the usual columns, or if N is not a positive whole number, the command exits with status 2 and writes no file. Otherwise it exits with status 0.

Add tests for the new feature.
